textbookBox.concept: The word pankha comes from pankh, which means the feather of a bird. Pankha is used for all fans and pankhi for a small plumed fan of ancient India.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 9 english · Winds of Change · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: Pankhas became cultural goods carried along trade routes, seen as exotic and stylish. Each village developed its own varieties, with distinct materials and designs.

beats.en: Pankhas became cultural goods carried along trade routes, seen as exotic and stylish. Each village developed its own varieties, with distinct materials and designs.
beats.speakEn: Pankhas became cultural goods carried along trade routes, seen as exotic and stylish. Each village developed its own varieties, with distinct materials and designs.

beats.en: In Rajasthan and Gujarat artisans make appliqué and mirror-work fans with cross-stitch embroidery. In Bengal, delicate fans are made from sola, the milky-white spongy centre of a water plant.
beats.speakEn: In Rajasthan and Gujarat artisans make appliqué and mirror-work fans with cross-stitch embroidery. In Bengal, delicate fans are made from sola, the milky-white spongy centre of a water plant.

textbookBox.concept: Palm leaf fans in Bengal are called Tal Patar Pankha and are easy to carry. In Uttar Pradesh the Phadh fans are adorned with gold and silver zari, silk and satin frills, and Bihar is known for bamboo

beats.en: Let us review the key takeaway from Winds of Change: Palm leaf fans in Bengal are called Tal Patar Pankha and are easy to carry. In Uttar Pradesh the Phadh fans are adorned with gold and silver zari, silk and satin frills, and Bihar is known for bamboo fans.
